candidate.answerReason: Under the recorded uniform interpretation, the probabilities of a negative and a positive draw are 2/3 and 1/3. Independence and the two disjoint same-sign cases give 4/9 + 1/9 = 5/9.

methods.label: Add the two same-sign probabilities
methods.explanation:
Use the standard interpretation that each draw is uniform on \([-20,10]\). A product is positive exactly when both numbers are negative or both are positive.

The whole interval has length \(30\). Its negative portion has length \(20\), and its positive portion has length \(10\), so a single draw is negative with probability \(2/3\) and positive with probability \(1/3\). Drawing exactly zero has probability zero because a single point has length zero.

Independence lets us multiply the probabilities for the two draws. The two favorable cases cannot occur together, so their probabilities add:
\[
P(\text{positive product})
=\left(\frac23\right)^2+\left(\frac13\right)^2
=\frac49+\frac19
=\boxed{\frac59}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
methods.levelReason: Only uniform interval lengths, signs of products, independence, and addition of disjoint probabilities are used.

methods.label: Compare favorable areas
methods.explanation:
Interpret both selections as uniform on \([-20,10]\). Represent the selected numbers by an ordered pair \((u,v)\). Because the selections are independent, the pair is uniform in the square
\[
[-20,10]\times[-20,10],
\]
whose area is \(30^2=900\).

The condition \(uv>0\) describes two disjoint regions. Both coordinates can be negative, giving a square of side \(20\), or both can be positive, giving a square of side \(10\). These have total area
\[
20^2+10^2=500.
\]
The coordinate axes are excluded because they give product zero; excluding these line segments does not change area. Thus
\[
P(uv>0)=\frac{500}{900}=\boxed{\frac59},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
methods.levelReason: The alternative uses only the coordinate plane and square areas to express the same elementary probability model.

candidate.annotationRationale: Uniform length or area ratios are the common target. The signed-product rule and explicit independence support both methods. The first method uses independent-event multiplication and disjoint addition; the second uses square areas and composite area. Inequality manipulation and finite equally likely point counting are not used.
limitations: The probability calculation uses the recorded convention that selection at random from the interval means uniform selection.

review.mathematicalCheck: Under the explicitly stated uniform interpretation, the sign probabilities are 2/3 and 1/3. Independence gives a positive-product probability of 4/9+1/9=5/9. Equivalently, favorable area is 400+100 out of 900; zero-product boundaries contribute no area.
review.levelCheck: Both explanations use accessible interval lengths, independence, and square areas.
review.methodDistinctness: Independent sign cases and planar area comparison provide useful distinct probability representations.
